Timing.description: Wall and CPU time and memory for one check, as measured by the executor.

cached.description: True when the result came from the result cache: the check did not run in this run, and the timing is that of reading the entry.
cached.title: Cached

cpu_seconds.description: CPU time while the check ran; approximate. For a check on a thread this is the whole process's, so work on other threads counts too, and `shared_with` says whether checks overlapped. For a check in a worker process it is the worker's own, and missing if the worker was killed or died.
cpu_seconds.title: Cpu Seconds

peak_memory_bytes.description: Peak resident memory while the check ran, found by sampling; approximate, and a short spike between samples is missed. For a check on a thread it is the whole process's, including the loaded data, and shared with any check that overlapped (`shared_with`). For a check in a worker process it is the worker's own, including what it mapped of the data.
peak_memory_bytes.title: Peak Memory Bytes

shared_with.description: How many other checks on threads ran at the same time as this one. While any did, `cpu_seconds` and `peak_memory_bytes` are the whole process's and cannot be told apart per check. Always 0 for a check in a worker process.
shared_with.title: Shared With

wall_seconds.description: Time the executor spent on the check, from its start.
wall_seconds.title: Wall Seconds

Timing.title: Timing

UnknownProfile.description: A column whose meaning could not be inferred.

content_hash.description: A 64-bit digest of the column's values in row order, as 16 hex digits; None when the values cannot be hashed. Equal hashes mark candidate duplicates only: they also need equal `physical_dtype` and a comparison of the values, because the digest is 64 bits and ignores the dtype.
content_hash.title: Content Hash

values_with_replacement_char.description: Values holding U+FFFD, the mark a lossy decode leaves; None unless the column holds strings.

post.description:
Queue a profiling run of the dataset's latest source. It runs with the
settings of that run, then the dataset's saved settings on top. The source is read
again, so a file that has gone fails the job.

get.description: A dataset's runs, newest first. The key is the dataset key, percent-encoded.

The settings saved for a dataset: the fields it overrides, `{}` when it has
none. The key is the dataset key, percent-encoded.

put.description:
Save a dataset's settings, replacing any earlier ones. The body holds
`ProfileConfig` fields; only those it sets are kept.

get.description: Jobs, the most recently requested first.

post.description:
Queue a profiling run of a local file. It runs after the jobs ahead of it,
and its run is stored when it ends; follow it with `getJob`.

get.description:
A job's state and its progress events numbered after `after`. The events end
with a `job_finished` event that names the run, when there is one.

post.description:
Cancel a job. A queued job is cancelled at once; a running one stops before
its next check, and is `running` until it does.
